tasks.short: Assess needs to inform curriculum development

steps.what: Gather needs assessments through interviews and checked group-level learning records
Calculate group summaries and compare coverage against curriculum requirements
Interpret needs evidence and prioritise curriculum development with stakeholders

tasks.design: Configure checked group-summary formulas in {SPREADSHEET}, reusing the coordinator's existing comparison table. Interviews, evidence validation and interpretation remain human; the summary does not assign learner levels or infer individual needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated tallying and formatting of group comparisons.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas and saved views can reproduce those calculations.
tasks.still_hard: A measured gap may reflect missing evidence, teaching context or an unsuitable measure.
tasks.human_edge: Hear needs absent from formal records and test competing explanations.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic with unchanged responsibility for curriculum priorities.

reach.task: Plan a curriculum improvement trial from the assessment
reach.learn: Sampling limits and the difference between need and measured attainment

evidence.claim: Checked group-summary formulas can reduce repetitive tallying without automating needs interpretation; savings are a scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is curriculum-level needs assessment, excluding individual grading, placement and teaching.

Coordinator produces the checked evidence and table in s1, capturing group label, reporting period, measure definition, numerator, denominator, missingness and curriculum topic. Full 45% capture and validation time remains. Existing record producers retain their work; no new teacher data entry is assumed. Missing or incomparable measures are reported as gaps and handled manually.
Test native summaries before custom code. No model clusters personal comments, no new individual learner scoring, and no saving from existing runtime.
unknowns: Time spent on calculation rather than interviews
research_questions: Do checked summaries shorten preparation while preserving missingness and sampling limitations?

already_counted.description: Check summary definitions and incomplete group fields

incremental.description: Maintain comparison formulas and measure definitions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=86; gross 14 minus upkeep 3 gives net 11. High assumes repeated comparable summaries; low assumes incomplete data consumes the gain. Interviews and interpretation retain 80 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define suitable instructional and learning objectives

steps.what: Clarify learning purpose, learner context and curriculum constraints
Draft instructional, learning or performance objectives and observable success criteria

loop.purpose: Propose objective wording aligned to the agreed brief
loop.input: Objective brief and permitted curriculum references
loop.output: Draft objectives with observable criteria and links to the brief
loop.check: Coordinator checks intended learning, appropriate challenge, observability and whether the wording introduces unsupported requirements
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, then manual wording for unsuitable objectives
loop.why_not_simpler: A verb list helps structure but cannot choose suitable wording from a varied educational brief

steps.what: Define final objectives after checking coherence, feasibility and curriculum alignment

tasks.design: Start with native objective templates in {DOCS}, then use bounded drafting for wording that varies by brief. The coordinator defines the final objectives and checks whether they describe worthwhile, feasible learning rather than merely easy-to-count activity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated phrasing of objectives from educational briefs.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can offer wording for explicit educational review.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what learners should achieve is a substantive educational decision.
tasks.human_edge: Reject an objective that is measurable but misses the intended learning.
tasks.altitude: Less initial wording work; educational decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design an activity aligned to an objective
reach.learn: Constructive alignment and observable evidence of learning

evidence.claim: Bounded drafting can propose objective wording; suitability and alignment still require coordinator judgement.

assumptions: Boundary starts from existing needs evidence and ends with objectives, excluding needs assessment, activity design and learner evaluation.

Coordinator produces the objective brief in s1 with topic, intended audience, prerequisites, purpose, constraints and curriculum source version. Full clarification and capture time remains. Missing purpose or contradictory requirements return to human clarification, not invented goals.
Test native templates before model use. No learner personal data, individual level assignment or automated performance evaluation is introduced.
unknowns: Share of objectives needing substantial rewriting
research_questions: Do draft objectives shorten wording time without narrowing the intended learning?

already_counted.description: Review objective meaning and remove unsupported requirements

incremental.description: Maintain objective examples and drafting constraints

approvals.approved_version: Exact objective wording, criteria, audience and curriculum reference version; any change requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=84; gross 16 less upkeep 3 gives net 13. High assumes useful first wording; low assumes unsuitable drafts consume the gain. Brief clarification and final definition retain 60 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design instructional aids for classroom or online use

steps.what: Select instructional objectives, approved content and aid format
Design instructional aids, examples and directions for the chosen format

loop.purpose: Draft instructional examples and directions from approved content
loop.input: Instructional aid brief and approved learning content
loop.output: Draft aid with examples, directions and source references
loop.check: Coordinator checks factual accuracy, objective alignment, accessibility, answer correctness and whether standalone directions are understandable
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; failed sections are designed manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout but varied examples and explanations need semantic drafting

steps.what: Test instructional aid usability and approve the final version

tasks.design: Use native {LMS} layouts before adding a bounded draft for examples and directions. The coordinator checks source accuracy and tests the actual aid, including standalone usability where no instructor will explain it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated drafting of examples and instructions from approved content.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing authoring tools can draft activities and adapt text for review.
tasks.still_hard: A polished aid may teach the wrong idea or be inaccessible in practice.
tasks.human_edge: Notice learner confusion that a formally correct answer key would miss.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft production with unchanged testing and release responsibility.

reach.task: Test an aid against actual classroom constraints

evidence.claim: LessonUp supports rewriting slide text by tone or level and generating word lists; Snappet can generate a classroom activity from a learning objective.
The savings allocation is a local trial scenario, not a transfer of teacher lesson-planning trial results.

assumptions: Boundary is aid design and approval, excluding objective-setting, routine teaching and learner assessment.

Coordinator produces format, audience, objective references, source versions and delivery constraints in s1; all selection time remains. Source gaps stop generation and require manual resolution. No personal learner data is needed.
Test native authoring and reusable layouts first. Trial and approval work retain all time; no extra teacher testing is assumed free or transferred outside this baseline.
unknowns: Existing authoring tools and accessibility requirements
research_questions: Do draft examples reduce design time after content and accessibility checks?

already_counted.description: Check draft examples, directions and source alignment

incremental.description: Maintain drafting constraints and reusable examples

approvals.approved_version: Exact aid revision, examples, directions, answer content and delivery format tested; any edit requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80; gross 20 less upkeep 3 gives net 17. High assumes useful source-grounded drafts; low assumes corrections consume drafting gains. Testing retains all 35 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design digital learning products and performance support

steps.what: Clarify learning product requirements and gather approved procedural content
Design navigation, instructional sequence and performance support interactions
Assemble the learning product from storyboard and approved assets
Test product paths, accessibility and procedural accuracy before handover

tasks.design: Reuse native {LMS} page and navigation templates to assemble a coordinator-designed storyboard. Keep instructional design and all path, accessibility and procedure testing human; the product is handed over for the existing release process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated page setup and asset placement after design decisions were made.
tasks.enabler_now: Native authoring templates can reuse layout and navigation settings.
tasks.still_hard: A technically working path can still fail the user's real learning or support need.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the right support at the point of difficulty rather than add more content.
tasks.altitude: Less page assembly with unchanged learning design and testing authority.

reach.task: Check product deployment and support requirements

evidence.claim: Native course-authoring templates can reduce repeated page assembly; this scenario does not automate instructional design.
Easygenerator supports drafting courses from existing documents; it demonstrates document-based authoring capability rather than a measured saving for this workflow.

assumptions: Boundary is learning-product design through tested handover, excluding source procedure ownership, software engineering and production publication.

Coordinator captures requirements in s1 and produces page sequence, content references, navigation targets and interaction decisions in s2, with both steps fully retained. Approved asset owners keep their existing production work. s3 retains asset mapping and manual handling of unsupported interactions; missing targets stop assembly rather than creating guessed paths.

Test native templates before custom code or model generation. No new asset creation is assumed free; any substantial custom interaction needs a separate scoped project. Existing runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Template coverage of actual learning products
research_questions: Does template reuse reduce page assembly after asset mapping and path checks?

already_counted.description: Map assets and handle template exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain reusable page and navigation templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=88; gross 12 minus upkeep 2 gives net 10. High assumes repeat layouts; low assumes custom interactions consume the assembly gain. Requirements, design and tests retain 80 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The coordinator retains learning decisions and testing while reducing repeated summaries, wording and assembly.
reach: Help teachers test instructional aids and learning administrators deploy usable products
role.ambitious_version: Design clearer learning support with traceable evidence and tested learner paths.
